title: Free Static File Hosting Sites — What Actually Works in 2026
meta_description: What does Free Static File Hosting Sites cost in 2026 (spoiler: nothing), and how do you set it up properly? Covers free tiers, open-source alternatives and…
intro: This is the kind of post The Free Stack exists to write: a practical, no-fluff guide to free static file hosting sites, assembled from free tiers, open-source projects and endpoints that ask for no API key at all.

We'll walk through Why Static Hosting Is Free, Github Pages, Cloudflare Pages, and Netlify Free Tier — and finish with the questions people actually ask, so you can check before you buy anything. You shouldn't have to buy anything.

sections.heading: Why Static Hosting Is Free
paragraphs: Skip the fluff and start here: Static sites are cheap to host because there is no server to keep awake — which is why so many hosts give the tier away.

The upshot: Files are cached at edge nodes and served from memory; there is no database, no runtime, no scaling. When the marginal cost of serving a page approaches zero, hosting becomes a feature to win signups — and that is the deal a personal blog gets to keep.
Keep it this simple and you'll be ahead of most tutorials out there.

sections.heading: Github Pages
paragraphs: Skip the fluff and start here: GitHub Pages is a free static-hosting service built directly into the repo that already hosts your code.

The upshot: Point Pages at any subdirectory of a repository and GitHub serves it over HTTPS with a built-in URL, custom domain support, and automatic deploys on every push. For a static blog the entire hosting bill is zero, with no server, no DNS glue, and no renewal dates.
If you only do one thing today, make it this one.
bullets: Pick a directory (e.g. autopilot-blog/site/) as the site source in repo Settings → Pages
Push (or let the engine push) the built HTML and the site deploys in under a minute
Optionally map a custom domain in the same settings page

sections.heading: Cloudflare Pages
paragraphs: Start with the basics. Cloudflare Pages is a free static hosting platform with a global CDN and preview deploys for every pull request.

The upshot: Connect a Git repo and every branch or PR gets its own preview URL, while the main branch gets a production URL on Cloudflare's network. The free tier covers static sites comfortably and custom domains are supported without a separate CDN bill.
If you only do one thing today, make it this one.
bullets: Create a Pages project in the Cloudflare dashboard and link the repo
Point the build output at the static folder
Add a custom domain in the project's domains tab

sections.heading: Netlify Free Tier
paragraphs: Worth spending ten minutes on: Netlify's free tier hosts a static site with SSL, CI/CD from Git, forms and generous bandwidth — no card required.

So what does that look like when you're actually doing it? Netlify is the classic pick for static sites: drag a folder in or connect a repo, and it handles builds, redirects, and TLS certificates automatically. The free plan's limits are far beyond what a personal blog ever needs.
If you only do one thing today, make it this one.

faq.question: What are the real limitations of free static file hosting sites?
faq.answer: GitHub Pages is a free static-hosting service built directly into the repo that already hosts your code. Treat that as the working assumption and re-check the docs once a quarter.

faq.question: Can I keep this free forever, or is it a trial?
faq.answer: Mostly, yes. Cloudflare Pages is a free static hosting platform with a global CDN and preview deploys for every pull request. The free tier is the product, not the teaser — but the paid tier exists for when you need slas, support or volume.

Don't forget — GitHub Pages is a free static-hosting service built directly into the repo that already hosts your code.
